correctness.rationale: At word length L the mechanical intercept cuts are the phases -iu for 0<=i<=L. On an interval avoiding collisions the ordered arcs can be followed continuously, and all L digit values are constant on each moving arc. At a cut only one ceiling argument changes and the ceiling convention takes its left-hand limiting word. Intercept density gives precisely these words for the irrational rotation; for reduced rational denominator Q>L the cuts lie on the Q-grid and each arc's right endpoint realizes its word as a shift of the rational mechanical word. For lower convergent p/q, ps-qr=1 with 1<=s<q makes beta=(p+r)/(q+s) reduced and gives p/q-beta=1/[q(q+s)]. Neither the interval from beta to p/q nor the interval from p/q to the upper preceding convergent has an interior reduced fraction of denominator less than q: in each unimodular endpoint basis, any interior fraction has two positive integer coefficients. Thus the length-(q-1) words are unchanged through alpha. Each prefix sum of each rational shift is at most ceil(m beta)<=ceil(m alpha); at the first differing digit this forces the correct lexicographic ordering. Rational digit average beta and irrational average alpha follow by telescoping and unique ergodicity. The cost is at most theta^(q-1) and the gain from digit deficit is greater than t/(2q^2), which wins for every fixed theta<1 and t>0 along unbounded lower convergents. At t=0 the zero set of the nonnegative distance is the uniquely ergodic closed subsystem. The digit potential has sup norm and Lipschitz seminorm at most one, giving the stated arbitrarily small perturbation.
residual_risks: The source's finite golden-slope samples do not establish arbitrary irrational slopes, full lexicographic admissibility, or a Lipschitz optimization theorem. These conclusions follow from the preceding mechanical-word and Farey arguments.

value.rationale: This identifies the loss of robustness at the zero digit coefficient despite unique maximization and gives a specified direction, finite-period witnesses and an explicit gain for every irrational slope. Avoiding an assumption on continued-fraction growth is substantive: the lower-convergent error alone need not provide polynomial separation from an exponentially small distance penalty.
residual_risks: The competitors need not maximize the perturbed potential. Neither pressure nor the perturbed maximizing-measure set is classified.
